courses.name: Introduction to Web Technology
courses.description: HTML structure, CSS layout fundamentals, JavaScript basics, DOM manipulation, and HTTP client-server concepts.

modules.title: HTML Structure & Semantics
modules.content: HTML provides the skeleton of a web page. Semantic tags like <header>, <main>, and <footer> give meaning to the structure, improving accessibility and SEO.

modules.title: CSS Layout Fundamentals
modules.content: CSS controls the visual presentation. We use Flexbox and CSS Grid to create responsive, modern layouts that adapt to different screen sizes.

modules.title: JavaScript Basics & DOM
modules.content: JavaScript adds interactivity. The Document Object Model (DOM) allows JS to read and change the content, structure, and style of a website dynamically.

modules.title: HTTP & Client-Server Concepts
modules.content: Understanding how the web works: clients (browsers) send requests to servers, and servers respond with data over the HTTP protocol.

courses.name: Hardware Fundamentals & Programming
courses.description: Computer hardware architecture, logic gates, truth tables, memory hierarchies, and introductory algorithmic problem solving.

modules.title: Computer Hardware Architecture
modules.content: The von Neumann architecture consists of the CPU, memory, and input/output devices. The CPU fetches, decodes, and executes instructions.

modules.title: Logic Gates & Truth Tables
modules.content: Basic building blocks of digital circuits: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR. Truth tables map all possible input combinations to their output.

modules.title: Memory Hierarchies
modules.content: From fastest/smallest to slowest/largest: Registers, Cache (L1/L2/L3), RAM, and Secondary Storage (SSD/HDD).

courses.name: Elementary Mathematics I
courses.description: Set theory, quadratic equations, polynomials, mathematical induction, trigonometry, and coordinate geometry.

modules.title: Set Theory & Logic
modules.content: A set is a well-defined collection of distinct objects. Operations include union (∪), intersection (∩), and complement (').

modules.title: Quadratic Equations
modules.content: Equations of the form ax² + bx + c = 0. Solved using factorization, completing the square, or the quadratic formula.

modules.title: Trigonometry
modules.content: Study of triangles. Key identities include sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, and the sine/cosine rules for non-right-angled triangles.

courses.name: Elementary Mathematics II
courses.description: Limits and continuity, derivatives of algebraic and trigonometric functions, integration techniques, and vector geometry.

modules.title: Functions of Real Variables
modules.content:
What is a Function?

A function f from set X (Domain) to set Y (Codomain) assigns exactly one element f(x) to every x in X.

Analogy: A function is like a vending machine. You press a button (input), and the machine gives you exactly one snack (output).

Key Concepts

  • Domain: All possible inputs that are allowed
  • Range: The actual outputs the function produces
  • Even Function: f(-x) = f(x) (mirrors over Y-axis, like x²)
  • Odd Function: f(-x) = -f(x) (180° rotation, like x³)
  • Periodic: f(x + T) = f(x) (repeats, like sin x with period 2π)
  • Composite: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x))

The Difference Quotient

Formula: [f(x+h) - f(x)]/h — represents the slope of a secant line. This is the precursor to derivatives!

modules.title: Limits & Limit Theorems
modules.content:
Why Limits?

Before calculus, we could calculate the slope of a straight line. But how do you find the slope of a curve at one exact point? The answer: bring two points closer and closer together and see what the slope approaches.

Analogy: Imagine walking toward a wall. You get closer and closer but never touch it. That prediction of where you'll end up is the limit.

Limit Theorems

  • Sum Rule: lim[f(x) + g(x)] = lim f(x) + lim g(x)
  • Product Rule: lim[f(x)·g(x)] = lim f(x) · lim g(x)
  • Quotient Rule: lim[f(x)/g(x)] = lim f(x) / lim g(x) (if denominator ≠ 0)
  • Squeeze Theorem: If g(x) ≤ f(x) ≤ h(x) and both bounds approach L, then f(x) → L

Indeterminate Forms

Forms like 0/0, ∞/∞ don't give clear answers. We resolve them using algebraic manipulation (factoring, rationalizing) or L'Hôpital's Rule (later).
